comparator.route: Frontiers in Medical Biology specialisation, followed by 12 EC of electives and the standard 18-EC Bachelor Project
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official curriculum accounts for 180 EC. Year 1 is a fixed 60-EC foundation in cells, genetics, microbes, animal form, anatomy, physiology, disease mechanisms, mathematics, statistics and academic skills. Year 2 is a fixed 60-EC programme in biochemistry, molecular and cell biology, immunology, molecular techniques, bioethics, biomedical data science, cellular imaging/regulation, omics and a mini-thesis. The HTML table prints a dash for Data Science, while the official 2026–27 curriculum PDF assigns it 3 EC; that PDF value completes the 60-EC year and is used here. For year 3, Frontiers in Medical Biology is selected under the broad-academic-identity rule because its molecular, genomic and experimental emphasis continues the programme's named biomedical-sciences identity more broadly than the Neurobiology or Patient Oriented Research alternatives. Its 30 EC comprise Frontiers in Medical Biology 1 (12), Frontiers in Medical Biology 2 (6), Practicum Experimental Genomics (6) and a 6-EC specialisation elective, followed by 12 EC of genuine electives and an 18-EC Bachelor Project.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The programme offers three named third-year specialisations. Frontiers in Medical Biology most directly continues the degree's cross-cutting molecular-cell biology, omics, systems-biology, disease-mechanism and experimental-research identity. Neurobiology narrows toward the nervous system, while Patient Oriented Research narrows toward clinical and patient-facing biomedical research.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad closest route covers human biology, disease mechanisms and biomedical research. Direct target evidence then supports distinct public-health/intervention and biomedical-data/omics alternatives. All three form coherent 24-course curricula, pass mechanical feasibility and differ by at least four courses per side. The separately supported Neurobiology direction cannot be added after the maximum of three.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both develop academic and professional direction, with UCR PPD covering a different and broader programme.
Both relate human anatomy to physiological function; UCR is organized by body regions and systems.
Both study pharmacological actions, effects and therapeutic use.
Both examine immune mechanisms and response to infection.
Both study cardiovascular pathophysiology; UCR covers multiple organ systems rather than only the heart and circulation.
Both teach biological neuroscience, with UCR not limited to human medical contexts.
Both introduce biomedical foundations from cells to body systems.
Both examine human cell structures and their function, although UCR is broader molecular cell biology.
Both study molecular biochemistry and metabolism.
Both address genetic mechanisms in human disease; UCR combines pathology and genetics.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Humane Ontwikkeling component; its 6 EC and compulsory or choice status remain explicit.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Microbiologie component; its 6 EC and compulsory or choice status remain explicit.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Humane Evolutie component; its 6 EC and compulsory or choice status remain explicit.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Medical Biochemistry component; its 6 EC and compulsory or choice status remain explicit.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Oncology component; its 6 EC and compulsory or choice status remain explicit.
UvA requires a dedicated first-year cell course; UCR distributes this material across its biomedical gateway and molecular-cell biology.
UvA's 12-EC cellular imaging and regulation component has no single UCR equivalent.
UvA requires an experimental-genomics practicum within the selected specialisation; UCR lacks a direct wet-lab equivalent.
Both address ethical reasoning; UCR ethics is broader than biomedical philosophy of science.
Both teach epidemiological study of disease risk and population-level evidence.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Biomedische Wetenschappen en de Maatschappij component; its 6 EC and compulsory or choice status remain explicit.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Vrije keuzeruimte / minor component; its 30 EC and compulsory or choice status remain explicit.
Both teach statistical research design, though UCR is general and not biomedical-specific.
Both introduce empirical research and statistics; UCR emphasizes human experimental methods.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Omics component; its 6 EC and compulsory or choice status remain explicit.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Bachelor Thesis Biomedical Sciences - Experimental component; its 24 EC and compulsory or choice status remain explicit.
UvA's biomedical data-science course is distributed across UCR statistics, programming and data-science courses.
UvA requires a dedicated biomedical mini-thesis; UCR develops research writing across advanced courses.

notes.text: UvA Biomedical Sciences requires a tightly integrated molecular, anatomical, physiological, microbiological, immunological, omics and laboratory sequence, followed by a formal 30-EC specialisation and an 18-EC research placement. UCR can assemble biomedical, public-health and quantitative-data programmes, but it does not duplicate the full wet-lab sequence, the dedicated omics line or the guaranteed research placement; shared rows indicate substantive overlap rather than equivalence.
